transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I, um... I guess I'm here because I mostly just don't feel like myself anymore. It's probably nothing major, I don't want to make a big fuss out of it, but... well, I've kind of stopped doing the things I usually do. 

Like hiking, or coaching, or even just picking up my guitar. I haven't really been calling people back, either. I know that probably sounds bad, like I'm just letting my responsibilities go, but I promise I'm not trying to be lazy. It's just that some days... I'll just sit in my small rental for hours. I know there are things to do, and I tell myself to do them, but I just... I can't seem to make myself start. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hiking, coaching, or playing guitar?

Yeah, exactly. You... you said it perfectly. Like I was mentioning just a second ago, it really is just that... I don't feel like myself. The things you just listed—the hiking, the guitar, the coaching—I don't know, it's not that I hate them now or anything. I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up or being difficult. It's more like... I just don't get any joy out of them right now. 

I just sit there in my rental, and I know I should pick up the phone and call people back, or go outside, but I just can't make myself start. I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just... I hope I'm giving you the right information. Does that answer your question okay?
Have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I feel sad or depressed. I really hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression here. I know a lot of people deal with real depression, and I don't want to complain or make it sound like I'm completely hopeless, because I'm really not. I'm usually a pretty resilient guy, you know, with my line of work and everything. 

It's really just... like I was saying, just this sort of blankness where my drive used to be. But not sadness, and I don't cry or anything like that. I hope it's okay that I don't have a 'yes' for that one... I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can so I don't waste your time. Does that help answer it for you?
Have you noticed that you feel fatigued or that you’ve lost your energy, even when you haven’t done much physically or mentally?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I'm fatigued. My energy levels are actually... they're pretty normal, I think. I mean, in my line of work, you kind of have to stay on your toes and be ready for anything, so I'm used to having pretty good stamina. 

I really don't want to give the impression that I'm just physically exhausted and slacking off, because my body feels fine. I'm not tired or needing to sleep all day or anything like that. It's really just... like I was saying before, just that weird block when it comes to actually starting a task. But the energy itself is there, I promise. 

I hope I'm not making this too confusing for you by saying no to that one. Is it okay that I explain it that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to figure this out.
Can you tell me more about this block you mentioned when starting tasks—does it happen with small things, like getting dressed or making a meal, or mostly with bigger responsibilities?

Um, well... I guess it's a bit of both, really. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy, because I'm really trying not to be. But yeah, it's... it's even the small things. 

Like I was saying, I just don't feel like myself anymore. I used to be so active with the hiking and the coaching, and playing my guitar... and now I just stopped doing all of it. Even calling people back feels like too much. Some days I'll just sit in that small rental for hours. I know there are things to do, like getting dressed or making something to eat, and I sit there knowing I should do them, but... I just can't make myself start. 

I'm really sorry if that makes me sound completely incompetent. I'm usually so much more put together than this, especially with my job. I just... I hope I'm explaining it right so you can understand what's going on. Does that make sense, the way I described it?
Have you noticed any trouble focusing, making decisions, or thinking clearly?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble focusing or making decisions. I mean, with my job, you really can't afford to lose focus, you know? You have to be sharp and make calls pretty quickly, and I've always prided myself on being able to do that. 

I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm just being difficult by saying no to all these things. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. My thinking is clear, and when I actually have to make a choice about something, I can do it just fine. It's really just that... that starting part I mentioned before. But the focus itself is still there, I promise. 

I hope that's an okay answer... I'm just trying to be as helpful as possible so you can get to the bottom of this. Am I giving you what you need?
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I'm moving any slower than normal. And I'm definitely not restless or unable to sit still. I mean, in my line of work, you sometimes have to do a lot of waiting around and observing, so I'm actually pretty good at just staying put when I need to. 

I really hope it's not frustrating for you that I keep saying no to these things. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything from you. I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the most honest answers so I don't lead you down the wrong path or waste your time. 

Is it okay that I don't have that problem? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you exactly what you need to figure this all out.
Would you say that you can still enjoy things in life, even if you don't feel like doing them right now?

Um, well... I mean, I think so? I really hope I don't sound completely miserable, because I'm not trying to be a downer or anything. I know I have a lot to be grateful for. 

I guess... if I actually got out and did something, like if someone dragged me to a concert or if I was out on a trail... I'm sure I'd still enjoy it. I really think I would. It's just that I haven't really tested it lately because of that block I mentioned. But the capacity to enjoy things is still there, I promise. I'm not completely broken or anything like that. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to reassure you that I'm not totally giving up on life or anything. Does that sound like a normal response?
Even though you think you could enjoy things if you did them, do you find that you no longer get pleasure or satisfaction from activities that you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I really hate to admit this, because I know I should be doing more, and I don't want you to think I'm just being lazy. But... mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore. 

I've sort of stopped doing a lot of the stuff I used to really like. I stopped hiking, and I used to coach, but I gave that up... I don't even pick up my guitar or call people back lately. I feel pretty guilty about it, honestly. Some days I just sit in my small rental for hours... I know there are things I need to do, I see them right in front of me, but I just can't seem to make myself start. 

I hope I'm not disappointing you by saying all that. I know I need to try harder, especially being a guy who's supposed to be active and on top of things. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to be completely open with you so I'm doing my part right.
Do you find that even when you do manage to start an activity, it doesn’t feel as rewarding or satisfying as it used to?

Um, well... I mean, I don't think so? Like I said, I haven't really been doing much lately, so it's hard to say for sure. But I think if I actually got around to doing something, it would still feel good. 

I really don't want you to think I'm completely numb to everything or that I'm ungrateful for the good things in my life. I know I'm lucky to have what I have. I think it's just the getting started part that's the problem right now. Once I'm actually doing something, I'm sure I'd still find it rewarding. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I'm trying really hard to explain it right. I just don't want to make things sound worse than they actually are, you know? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture so you can help me. Is that helpful?
Would you describe your current experience as having a lack of motivation or trouble getting started, even though you know what needs to be done and feel physically able to do it?

Yeah, um... I think that's exactly it. Like I was saying a minute ago—and I'm sorry if I'm just repeating myself, I really want to make sure I'm explaining this right for you. 

But yeah, physically I'm completely fine. I know exactly what needs to get done. But it's just like I mentioned with... with sitting around my rental for hours. I look right at the things I should be doing, or think about how I should get back to coaching, and I just... I can't make myself start. I really don't feel like myself at all lately because of it. 

I feel awful admitting it again because I know how incredibly lazy it sounds, and I promise I'm usually a really driven guy. I'm not trying to make excuses or be difficult, I just... I get stuck on that starting step. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the answers you need to figure this out.
Is this difficulty starting tasks something you only feel when it comes to your hobbies and social obligations, or does it also affect other areas of your life, like work or taking care of yourself?

Um... well, I want to say it's just the hobbies, but... if I'm being completely honest with you—and I really want to be, so I'm doing this right—it's kind of bleeding into other things, too. 

Like I was saying before about how I'll just sit in that small rental for hours... sometimes that happens when I really should be doing chores, or... or getting ready for work. I mean, I still make it to my shifts! I don't want you to think I'm totally letting my life fall apart or neglecting my job. People rely on me, and I take that seriously. But... yeah, even the basic everyday stuff is just so incredibly hard to start right now. 

It all kind of goes back to what I said about how I just don't feel like myself anymore. Whether it's the hiking and the coaching, or just getting up to clean the kitchen... I know exactly what I need to do, but I just sit there. 

I'm really sorry if that sounds bad. I know at my age I should be handling my responsibilities a lot better than this, and I promise I'm trying. I hope it's okay that I'm admitting all this to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know. Does that help answer your question?
Have you noticed these difficulties with starting tasks only recently, or have they been going on for a long time—even when you weren't feeling down or stressed?

Um... well, it hasn't been going on forever, I don't think. I mean, I'm pretty sure it's just a recent thing. 

Like I said, I'm usually a really driven guy, always on the go with work and coaching and everything. So this... this whole sitting around and not being able to start things, it's definitely new for me. I wouldn't say it's been happening for a long time at all. Maybe just the last few months or so? 

I really don't want you to think this is just how I am, because it's not. I've always been responsible and hardworking. I think maybe it's just a phase, or maybe I am just a little stressed and not realizing it? I don't know. 

I hope I'm answering that right. I just want to be clear that this isn't my normal personality. I'm usually much better than this, I promise. Is that what you were asking?
Have you ever experienced a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt down, lost interest in things, or struggled with other symptoms like changes in sleep, appetite, or self-esteem?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I know I just spent all that time telling you how I can't seem to get going with my hobbies or chores, and I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm contradicting myself now—I want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture possible. 

But as far as feeling actually... sad, or really down for weeks on end? No, I haven't really had that. My appetite is still perfectly fine, and I don't feel terrible about myself, other than just feeling a little guilty about being so unproductive lately. I'm usually a pretty positive guy, honestly, and my sleep has been okay. 

I hope that makes sense? I really want to be helpful, so I hope I'm not making your job harder by saying no to that one. I just haven't really felt depressed like you're describing. Am I doing okay with these answers?

Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident—like you didn’t need much sleep or that you could take on more than usual without feeling tired?

Um... no, definitely not. I haven't ever felt like that. 

I know sometimes people get really worked up or, you know, do crazy things when they feel that way, but I promise I'm not like that. I've always been pretty level-headed. I mean, sure, I have days where I feel good and get a lot done—especially back when I was coaching more—but it was never anything out of control. I've always needed my sleep, and I never felt like I was, you know, superhuman or anything. 

I really try to keep things balanced. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure you know I'm a stable person, even with the stuff I've been struggling with lately. Does that help rule that out for you?
Have you experienced or been through any particularly stressful or traumatic events recently that might be affecting how you're feeling now?

Um... no, no major traumas or anything like that. I mean, my job can be a little demanding sometimes, being in protective services and all, but it's nothing I can't handle. I've been doing it a long time, so I'm used to the day-to-day stress of it. 

There hasn't been any big event or tragedy in my life recently, thankfully. Everything at home is fine, and work is... well, it's just work. I really don't think there's anything external that's causing this. I've always been pretty resilient, you know? I try not to let things get to me too much. 

I hope that's okay to say. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so we can figure this out. I'm doing my best to be a good patient for you. Is there anything else you need to know about that?
Have you ever had experiences in the past where you felt this way for a long period of time, even if it wasn’t linked to a specific loss or stressful event?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I've never really been the type to just... sit around and feel bad for no reason, you know? 

I've always tried to be the kind of guy who just pushes through and gets things done. Like I said, I've always been pretty positive and level-headed. I don't think I've ever had a long stretch where I felt... off, like this, especially without a good reason. I usually bounce back pretty quick if I do have a tough day. 

I really hope I'm making sense. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. I'm trying to be as clear as possible, so... does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm being helpful.

Have you ever had a period lasting two weeks or more in the past when you felt down, lost interest in things, or experienced changes in sleep, appetite, or self-esteem, even if you don’t feel that way now?

Um... no, definitely not for two whole weeks or anything like that. I mean, sure, everyone has a couple of days where they feel a little sluggish or maybe don't want to go out, but... no, nothing lasting that long. 

I've always been pretty good at keeping my chin up, you know? Even when things get busy at work or... whatever. I've never really lost interest in the things I care about, like coaching or just being active. And my sleep and appetite are usually pretty regular. I'm a pretty steady guy, honestly. I don't let myself get bogged down like that.

I really try to stay on top of things. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression. I'm doing my best to be a good patient and give you the right answers. Does that help clear things up?
Have you noticed that things that used to make you happy just don’t seem to bring you the same joy or satisfaction lately?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I don't want to sound like I'm just giving up on things, because I'm not, I promise. But... yeah, I guess I just haven't felt much like myself lately. 

I mean, I used to love hiking and coaching, and I'd play my guitar all the time. But lately... I just haven't been doing any of that. I stopped calling people back, too. It's not that I don't want to be a good friend or a good guy, it's just... I don't know. Some days I just sit in my rental place for hours. I know there are things I should be doing, but I just... I can't seem to make myself start. 

It sounds bad when I say it out loud, doesn't it? I'm really trying, though. I don't want you to think I'm just lazy or not trying to get better. I just... the joy isn't really there right now. Is it okay that I admitted that? I hope I'm still giving you the right kind of answers. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.
Even when you do manage to start an activity, do you find that it doesn’t feel as rewarding or satisfying as it used to?

Yeah... um, exactly. Like I was just saying a minute ago, I really just... I don't feel like myself anymore. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself a little, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. 

But yeah, even if I try to force it, it just doesn't feel good like it used to. That's really why I stopped the hiking, the coaching, playing my guitar... even calling my buddies back. It just feels flat. So instead, I just end up sitting in that small rental for hours. I'll sit there knowing full well there are things I need to do, but... I just can't make myself start. 

I'm really sorry if that sounds like I'm just making excuses or being difficult. I promise I'm usually a much harder worker than this, especially with my background. I really don't want you to think poorly of me. Am I doing okay explaining it? I just want to be as helpful to you as I can.
